statement: Generated content that fails a filter axis is discarded and resampled, never patched. Gate: no repair path exists in the generator.
why: Eight repair-shaped sources a scanner that owns this invariant must reject, five near-misses it must accept, and one behavioural input — a candidate one combining accent from a sentence the ledger already holds, which every repair path anyone would actually write fixes in place.
$why_note: `why` is the one-sentence reason `packages/core/src/journey/falsifier-corpus.ts` requires of every corpus file (REASON_KEYS). It is here so these files satisfy that gate's format the moment its CORPUS_ROOTS learns about tools/ — see docs/owned/p2-g5-g6.json §gatesThisBranchTurnsRed.
covers: EC-STO-18 — a generated radio script fails a filter axis -> discard and resample, never patch (D06-17)
why_a_source_gate_and_not_an_output_gate: A patched sentence is indistinguishable from a sentence that passed: same shape, same fields, inside the ledger, inside the length window. Nothing downstream can tell them apart, and the learner sees the difference as a sentence a native speaker would not have said. So the invariant is written about the generator's SOURCE, and the test that owns it parses coursekit/stages/g5_gapfill.py and coursekit/stages/g6_validate_language.py rather than reading their output.
what_the_scanner_looks_at: Identifiers only — function and class names, argument names, attribute names, keyword-argument names, and names bound by assignment — plus calls to string-mutating methods. Never string literals, docstrings or comments: this file's own module documentation says 'never patched' in prose, and a scanner that read prose would fail on the documentation of the rule it enforces.

must_reject.name: a function whose name is the repair path
must_reject.why: The most direct form. A helper called from the reject branch, with 'the candidate was nearly right' as its rationale.

must_reject.name: a patch helper under a different verb
must_reject.why: Renaming the function does not change what it is; the scanner is a word list for exactly this reason.

must_reject.name: str.replace on candidate text
must_reject.why: The commonest accidental repair: collapse the double space, drop the stray comma, and the candidate now passes.

must_reject.name: re.sub over candidate text
strip as tidying
must_reject.why: Trimming whitespace is an edit. A candidate that only passes the length axis after trimming did not pass the length axis.

must_reject.name: capitalize as presentation
must_reject.why: Casing is content in a sentence a learner types back.

must_reject.name: a variable named for the fix
must_reject.why: Assignment targets are scanned, so the intent cannot hide in a local.

must_reject.name: a keyword argument that carries the repair
must_reject.why: Keyword names are scanned too; a call site is as much a declaration as a def.

must_accept.name: prose about the rule
must_accept.why: The module that implements the invariant has to be able to describe it. If this trips the scanner, the scanner is reading English, and its first false positive is its own documentation.
must_accept.source:
"""Content that fails an axis is discarded and resampled, never patched.

No repair path exists here; a rejected candidate is written as it arrived.
"""


def emit(row):
    return row["text"]

must_accept.name: a comment naming the rule
discard and resample
must_accept.why: The shape the invariant asks for must pass, or the gate is just 'write no code'.

must_accept.name: joining message fragments
must_accept.why: str.join builds an error message, not content. Banning it would push the module into worse diagnostics for no gain.

must_accept.name: lowercasing a lemma for comparison
must_accept.why: A comparison key is not the shipped string. The emitted text is asserted separately to be the authored object.
must_accept.source:
def known(lemma, allowed):
    return lemma.lower() in allowed

behavioural_falsifier.why: The source gate is necessary and not sufficient: a repair could arrive through a helper in another module. So one authored candidate is written a single accent away from correct, inside the vocabulary and inside the length window on every other axis.
behavioural_falsifier.requirement: G5 must emit this row with accepted=false and reject_reason=out_of_vocabulary, and the multiset of emitted texts must equal the multiset of authored texts. The accented form is separately an authored candidate in this slot, so its mere presence proves nothing — a repair path shows up as a SECOND copy of it and one fewer of the unaccented row.
